_purpose: Single house vocabulary backing the communication contract (research/communication-contract.md): rule L3 (gloss on first use in reader-facing artifacts) and the L12 term-choice law (reuse, borrow, coin) in its addendum. One source, many render points: the crux mirror, decision-card tooltips, the dashboard render, the case-study renderer, and clarity-lint all read or derive from this file.
_schema: v2 (additive). Per entry: gloss (one clause, plain words, <= 25 words, no ids, no score shorthand, no house-only coinages from other entries; pattern keys exempt from the id/score scans because they define those patterns); variants (exact strings the lint also matches, including deprecated spellings); known_equivalent (the established external name for the same or nearest concept, or null); anchor (ONE stable https URL defining the known concept - prefer en.wikipedia.org, rfc-editor.org, ISO, vendor canon; no implementation artifacts in paths - or null); anchor_waiver (required one-line reason when a house-only entry has anchor null); status (preferred | house-only | deprecated-alias-of:<headword>); first_defined (optional provenance: hypothesis id or artifact path where coined). v1 entries stay loadable: absent fields default to known_equivalent null, anchor null, status house-only.
_admission: The naming law for new terms, in strict order: (1) if a known term fits, the known term is the headword and any house coinage for the same concept enters as deprecated-alias-of it; (2) a house term that stays anchors externally to the nearest well-known concept so a glance gives context; (3) every gloss passes the gloss lint - the glossary itself reads plain. Entries land agent-drafted, maintainer-ratified.
_status_semantics: preferred: the headword IS the known or plain name (borrowed like andon, or plain English in its ordinary sense); free to use, gloss-on-first-use still applies in reader-facing modes. house-only: a coinage with no adequate known name; legal only with gloss on first use; must carry known_equivalent plus anchor or anchor_waiver; density counted per artifact (title ceiling: max 1). deprecated-alias-of:<headword>: never written in new artifacts; any use is a finding naming the canonical headword; old write-once artifacts are never edited - the alias entry is the tombstone a reader resolves through.
_source: v1: insider terms surfaced by the 2026-08-28 decision-clarity audit. v2 upgrade + additions: the 2026-08-29 artifact-language census (live unregistered coinages) under the maintainer language-integrity directive.

lane.gloss: one experiment's full pipeline (write-up, runs, scoring, verdict) executed by automated agents
lane.known_equivalent: pipeline run (one experiment, end to end)

wave.gloss: a batch of experiments run together toward one release version

ship.gloss: commit and publish so it is live for users

keep.gloss: final verdict: the tested change passed its pre-declared checks and is adopted as standard practice

discard.gloss: final verdict: the idea failed its checks and is dropped

refine.gloss: final verdict: partial pass — revise the idea and run it again

verdict.gloss: the mechanical keep/discard/refine outcome computed from checks declared before the run

counted run.gloss: a run whose scores count toward the verdict (practice or broken runs are excluded)
counted run.known_equivalent: valid trial (scores count toward the outcome)
counted run.anchor_waiver: no single established page separates counted from voided trials; the nearest concept is named in known_equivalent

void.gloss: a run thrown out before scoring; it counts neither for nor against

sweep.gloss: one automated pass applying the same check or fix across many items

gap.gloss: a found mismatch between what was claimed or planned and what actually exists

fixture.gloss: the input set an experiment runs against, locked before the run starts

frozen.gloss: locked against edits once registered; changing it invalidates the result

arm.gloss: one of the compared conditions in an experiment (like treatment vs control)

armed default.gloss: a pre-committed action that fires automatically on a named trigger unless vetoed first

preflight.gloss: automated checks run before launch to catch setup mistakes

pair economics.gloss: the cost/benefit of running the same task twice in parallel to compare outcomes

gate.gloss: an automated check that can block work until it passes

report-only.gloss: the check logs violations but blocks nothing

enforcing.gloss: the check actually blocks violations instead of just logging them

hook.gloss: a script that runs automatically around tool actions to enforce a rule

advisory.gloss: a non-blocking warning shown to working sessions

lint.gloss: a mechanical text or code check with a pass/fail result

ledger.gloss: the append-only file listing commitments and open items; one entry per line

row.gloss: one entry in the lab's open-items file

fragment.gloss: one write-once journal entry recording what happened and why

canon.gloss: the repository's authoritative rules and write-ups; changing it requires the maintainer

spec.gloss: the written experiment plan, including its pass/fail checks, fixed before running

zero-run spec.gloss: a registered experiment plan that has not run yet
zero-run spec.known_equivalent: preregistered study that has not yet run

supersede.gloss: replace an old item with a new one, leaving a pointer from old to new

amendment.gloss: a tracked edit to an already-registered experiment plan

bracket.gloss: a pre-registered follow-up that opens automatically when a result lands (if the result passes, then ...)

grade.gloss: scoring one run against its pre-declared checks

board.gloss: the maintainer-facing decision list (or, in design experiments, the rendered diagram under review — say which)

calibrated.gloss: verified against known-answer cases before live use

orchestrator.gloss: the automated session that schedules experiment runs and applies the verdict rules

ruling.gloss: a recorded decision, by the maintainer or the automation, that later work cites

triage.gloss: sorting open questions into: handle automatically, test instead, or genuinely needs a human

blast radius.gloss: everything a change can affect beyond the lab, especially other people

live surface.gloss: anything outside the lab that real people see or depend on

two-way door.gloss: a reversible decision — anything that lands as a commit can be undone, so it should not wait on a human

one-way door.gloss: an irreversible decision — it cannot be undone, so a human makes it

scratch repo.gloss: a throwaway repository used only for a test

round-trip.gloss: write it out, read it back, and verify nothing changed

parity.gloss: two implementations produce identical results on the same input

kept bundle.gloss: the exact set of files an experiment proved out, preserved at its passing state

lineage.gloss: a sequence of commits treated as one unit of history

re-sign.gloss: add the maintainer's cryptographic signature to existing commits after the fact

device flow.gloss: a login where a human types a short code shown on one device into another

NEEDS-IAN.gloss: flagged as requiring the maintainer personally
NEEDS-IAN.anchor_waiver: repo-local escalation label naming this lab's maintainer; no external page defines it

stagger.gloss: deliberately delaying runs so they do not overlap

WIP cap.gloss: a limit on how much work may be in progress at once

retrofit.gloss: applying a new rule to already-existing items

crux.gloss: the plugin's former name, replaced by Hyp Machine after a blind naming study

plugin.gloss: an installable extension package for Claude Code

score notation.gloss: NxM/M means: passed M of M checks in each of N scored runs (2x5/5 = all 5 checks passed in both runs)
score notation.anchor_waiver: house notation fully defined by its own gloss; pattern key (exempt from gloss id/score scans)

wall clock.gloss: elapsed real-world time, as opposed to compute time

decoy.gloss: a planted non-problem used to test for false alarms

drift.gloss: unintended divergence between two copies that should stay identical

H-NNN.gloss: a numbered testable idea with pass/fail checks declared before any run (an experiment id)
H-NNN.anchor_waiver: this repo's id grammar; pattern key (exempt from gloss id/score scans)

DEC-NNN.gloss: a numbered open question waiting on the maintainer (a decision id)
DEC-NNN.anchor_waiver: this repo's id grammar; pattern key (exempt from gloss id/score scans)

N-id.gloss: a numbered design-note item, not yet an experiment (N5, N13, ...)
N-id.anchor_waiver: this repo's id grammar; pattern key (exempt from gloss id/score scans)

K-strikes.gloss: after K failed relaunches an automated gate stops retrying the experiment and flags it for the maintainer

andon.gloss: a tripwire that halts related work and summons the maintainer when a defect class fires

muri.gloss: overload from asking one worker or window to carry more concurrent work than it can absorb

conwip.gloss: a scheduling rule admitting new work only when an item in progress finishes, keeping total load constant

tranche.gloss: one named batch of related work items planned and shipped together

observatory.gloss: the live status view showing in-flight experiment runs and their evidence

frontier.gloss: the queue of work items currently eligible to launch, across all planned batches

chain.gloss: a scripted sequence of unattended agent steps (run, score, verdict) executed one after another

quarantine.gloss: set a failing item aside, blocked from relaunch, until the maintainer reviews it

blip.gloss: a transient infrastructure failure during a run, recorded and retried without voiding the result

doctrine.gloss: a standing taught rule that agents must apply without being reminded

headword.gloss: the canonical form under which a glossary entry is listed; variants map to it
